messages.content: 計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning:
The user says: "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" They want to calculate something about hypothesis testing? They mention sample mean 98.2, sample std dev 1.4, sample size 40, null hypothesis mean 98.6. They ask to compute the standard deviation? Actually they say "計算...的零假設檢定的標準差" maybe they want to compute the standard error or the standard deviation of the sampling distribution? Or compute the p-value? The question: "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" Might be asking to compute the standard error of the mean difference? Let's parse: They have sample mean 98.2, sample std dev 1.4, sample size 40. Null hypothesis mean 98.6. They want to compute the standard deviation of the zero hypothesis test? That might refer to the standard error of the sample mean under the null? Actually the standard error of the sample mean is sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). So that's 1.4 / sqrt(40) ≈ 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2215. But maybe they want the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean difference? That would be sqrt((sample_std_dev^2)/sample_size + (population_std_dev^2)/population_size)? But we don't know population std dev. So likely they want the standard error.

But the phrase "以得到人口平均值為98.6" means "to get the population mean of 98.6". They might want to compute the p-value for a one-sample t-test with null mean 98.6. So we can compute t-statistic: t = (sample_mean - population_mean) / (sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size)). Then compute p-value. Let's do that: t = (98.2 - 98.6) / (1.4 / sqrt(40)) = (-0.4) / (1.4 / 6.3249) = (-0.4) / 0.2215 = -1.805. Degrees of freedom df = sample_size - 1 = 39. For a two-tailed test, p-value = 2 * P(T > |t|). We can approximate using t-distribution. For df=39, t=1.805. Using t-table: For df=40, t critical values: t0.05=2.021, t0.10=1.684. Our t=1.805 lies between 1.684 and 2.021. So p-value between 0.10 and 0.05. Roughly p ≈ 0.08. So p-value ~0.08. So we fail to reject null at alpha=0.05 but reject at alpha=0.10.

Thus answer: Standard error = 0.2215, t-statistic = -1.805, p-value ≈ 0.08. Provide explanation. Use the tool to compute p-value. Let's call the function.
